stem: A nurse plans to obtain an oral temperature from a client who has just finished drinking an iced beverage. Which action is appropriate?

options.A: Wait before measuring orally because recent hot or cold intake can produce an inaccurate reading.
options.B: Measure immediately because beverage temperature does not affect sublingual temperature readings.
options.C: Assume the oral route is always the most accurate route regardless of recent intake or client condition.
options.D: Avoid the oral route permanently because oral temperature measurement is inappropriate in all clinical settings.

rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI nursing guidance states that recently consumed hot or cold food or beverages can falsely raise or lower an oral temperature. The cited nursing skills guidance recommends waiting 15–25 minutes after hot or cold intake before oral measurement. B ignores a known measurement artifact. C overstates one route as universally superior. D is incorrect because the oral route is appropriate for many cooperative clients when contraindications and interfering factors are absent.
educational_objective: For accurate oral temperature measurement, recognize that recent hot or cold intake can distort the reading and allow an appropriate waiting period before obtaining the measurement.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_document_title: Nursing Skills — General Survey; Nursing Assistant — Demonstrate Reporting and Documentation of Client Data
source_locator: Nursing Skills, General Survey — Oral Temperature: recent hot/cold food or beverage can cause falsely elevated or decreased readings; oral temperature should be taken 15–25 minutes after hot/cold intake. Nursing Assistant, Oral Temperature section states the same timing and explains the sublingual route's susceptibility to recent intake.
source_claim_supported: Recent hot or cold oral intake can alter oral temperature measurements; waiting before measurement improves accuracy.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: obtain basic physiologic measurements accurately and provide routine care adapted to client condition.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — accurate oral temperature measurement
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item into a concrete bedside measurement decision and replaced the vague 15–30-minute claim with the directly located 15–25-minute nursing-text guidance. The answer itself avoids unnecessary numeric cueing while the rationale preserves the sourced interval.

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current NCBI nursing skills texts with an exact oral-temperature locator.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reflects the known measurement artifact. B denies it. C makes an unsupported universal route claim. D falsely excludes a commonly used route.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; wait before oral measurement after an iced beverage.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; recent intake can alter the reading.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; route selection depends on patient and clinical factors.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; oral measurement is appropriate in many settings.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A responds correctly to the specified recent cold intake.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern route accuracy and timing.
audit_findings.blueprint: Routine vital-sign measurement fits Basic Care and Comfort.
